sentences.text: I don't know who made you the boss.

alts.text: Who put you in charge?
I am not sure who decided that you would be the one in charge.

sentences.note: **made you the boss**는 남이 이래라저래라 할 때 "네가 뭔데 시켜?" 하고 받아치는 말이에요. 친구끼리 반쯤 농담으로도 많이 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 우리도 입양할 때 똑같은 일 겪었어.
sentences.text: We went through the same thing when we were adopting.

alts.text: Same thing happened to us when we adopted.
We experienced exactly the same situation during our adoption.

sentences.note: **went through the same thing**은 상대가 힘든 일을 털어놓을 때 "나도 그거 겪어 봤어" 하고 공감해 주는 말이에요. 뒤에 when을 붙여 언제였는지 말하면 돼요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그냥 우리가 아는 여자 중에 포커 칠 줄 아는 사람이 없을 뿐이야.
sentences.text: Yeah, we just don't happen to know any women that know how to play poker.

alts.text: Guess we don't know any girls who play poker.
It simply so happens that we do not know any women who know how to play poker.

sentences.note: **don't happen to know**는 "일부러 그런 건 아니고 어쩌다 보니 모른다"는 뜻이에요. 오해받을 때 "우리가 그러려고 한 게 아니라" 하고 변명하는 자리에서 써요.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 1 | Friends

sentences.ko: 저기, 원하면 어떻게 할지 정할 때까지 우리 집에 둬도 돼.
sentences.text: Look, if you want, you can keep it at our place until you find out what to do with it.

alts.text: You can leave it at our place till you figure it out.
If you would like, you are welcome to store it at our home until you decide what to do with it.

sentences.note: **keep it at our place**는 "우리 집에 맡겨 둬"라는 말이에요. 영어에서는 집을 house보다 **our place**라고 하는 일이 훨씬 많아요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 근데 나 화장한 거 그 사람이 눈치채지 않을까?
sentences.text: But won't she notice I have makeup on?

alts.text: She's gonna see my makeup, right?
Will she not notice that I am wearing makeup?

sentences.note: 화장을 하고 있다는 말은 **have makeup on**이라고 해요. 옷도 마찬가지로 have a jacket on처럼 써요. **won't she notice**는 "들키지 않을까?" 하고 걱정할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그냥 그 여자랑 사귀어 보지 그래?
sentences.text: Why don't you just go out with her?

alts.text: Just ask her out already.
Perhaps you should simply ask her on a date.

sentences.note: **Why don't you just** 는 상대가 망설일 때 답답한 마음으로 '그냥 ~하지 그래?' 하고 권하는 말입니다. **go out with** 는 '같이 나가다'가 아니라 '사귀다, 데이트하다'라는 뜻으로 씁니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 그럼 축하하러 어디 근사한 데 가나 보네.
sentences.text: So, you must be going somewhere fancy to celebrate.

alts.text: Going someplace nice to celebrate, huh?
I assume you are going somewhere elegant to celebrate.

sentences.note: **must be going** 은 '~하나 보네' 하고 눈치로 짐작할 때 씁니다. 좋은 식당 같은 곳은 **somewhere fancy** 라고 하면 딱 맞습니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends

sentences.text: You want me to wash my hands first, don't you?

alts.text: Wash up first, right?
I take it you would like me to wash my hands first.

sentences.note: **You want me to** 는 상대 표정을 보고 '나더러 ~하라는 거지?' 하고 속뜻을 짚을 때 씁니다. 끝에 **don't you?** 를 붙이면 '그렇지?' 하고 다짐을 받는 느낌이 됩니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones That Make You Laugh: Part 3 | Friends

sentences.text: I I know what you guys are going to say.

alts.text: Don't say it, I already know.
I am aware of what you are all about to say.

sentences.note: **I know what you guys are going to say** 는 잔소리나 반대가 나올 것 같을 때 먼저 막는 말입니다. 여럿에게 말할 때는 **you guys** 가 아주 흔합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 5 | Friends

sentences.ko: 잠깐 나랑 이리 좀 와 볼래?
sentences.text: Will you come here with me for a minute?

alts.text: Got a sec? Come with me.
Could you please come with me for a moment?

sentences.note: **for a minute** 은 '잠깐'이라는 뜻입니다. 여럿이 있는 자리에서 한 사람만 따로 불러내 얘기하고 싶을 때 이렇게 말합니다.
sentences.situation: The Ones with the Whole Gang from Season 10 | Friends
